newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norwegian shares edge higher, direction seen up.
newsitem.headline: Norwegian shares edge higher, direction seen up.

text.p: Norwegian share prices moved in a narrow range on Monday but held in positive territory and dealers said they expected further gains in the week ahead.
Firmer overseas markets and a decline in domestic short interest rates helped buoy the market, they said.
The Total share index closed 0.49 percent up at 1,101.16 points, the first time it has closed above the 1,100-point mark since February 25. Turnover was just over one billion crowns.
Dealers said apparent heavy business of 144 million crowns in construction and engineering group Kvaerner was linked to the expiry of options.
Insurance company Storebrand climbed another 0.80 crowns to close at 48.30 crowns, although dealers said fundamentally the stock was at full price.

Interest in Norway's largest insurer has been high since a mystery buyer entered the market searching for large blocks of stock. Norwegian billionaire Kjell Inge Roekke announced last Friday he had purchased six percent of the group for private investment. --Oslo newsroom, +47 22 42 50 41
